'''Tibor Juhasz''' is an [[Americans|American]]-[[Hungarians|Hungarian]] [[physicist]] and [[Entrepreneurship|entrepreneur]].<ref name="es">{{Cite web|url=https://engineering.uci.edu/users/tibor-juhasz|title=Tibor Juhasz &#124; Samueli School of Engineering at UC Irvine|website=engineering.uci.edu}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=About ViaLase {{!}} Leaders in Non-Invasive Glaucoma Treatment |url=https://www.vialase.com/about/ |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=Vialase |language=en-US |archive-date=2024-12-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241202144836/https://www.vialase.com/about/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He is a [[professor]] of [[ophthalmology]] and [[biomedical engineering]] at the [[University of California, Irvine School of Medicine]],<ref name="es" /> as well as the [[President (corporate title)|President]] and [[Chief technology officer|CTO]] of the medical device company ViaLase.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=UC Irvine - Faculty Profile System |url=https://www.faculty.uci.edu/profile/?facultyId=7004 |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=www.faculty.uci.edu |language=en}}</ref>

Juhasz is best known for his work on [[Laser medicine|medical applications of lasers]].<ref name="qwe">{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=b9IOU3oAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=sra|title=Tibor Juhasz - Google Scholar|access-date=2023-11-16|archive-date=2023-11-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116091710/https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=b9IOU3oAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=sra|url-status=live}}</ref> He and ophthalmology professor Ron Kurtz are the inventors of IntraLASIK, a device which uses [[Mode locking|femtosecond lasers]] to prepare the eye for [[LASIK]] surgery. IntraLASIK has since become standard procedure when performing LASIK surgery.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2024-03-27 |title=Invention to Impact: The story of LASIK eye surgery {{!}} NSF - U.S. National Science Foundation |url=https://www.nsf.gov/science-matters/invention-impact-story-lasik-eye-surgery |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=www.nsf.gov |language=en}}</ref> Juhasz has also developed similar devices to treat [[cataract]]s and [[glaucoma]].<ref name=":2" />

Juhasz has also founded several companies to commercialize his inventions.<ref name="ase">{{Cite web|url=https://www.vialase.com/|title=Vialase ® &#124; Redefining Glaucoma Treatment|website=Vialase|access-date=2023-11-16|archive-date=2023-11-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116091710/https://www.vialase.com/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> Two of his companies, IntraLase and LenSx, were later acquired by major medical device companies for hundreds of millions of dollars.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Alcon to Acquire LenSx Lasers, Inc. |url=https://optics.org/press/17 |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=optics.org |archive-date=2026-03-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260315015602/https://optics.org/press/17 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite news |title=AMO's IntraLase Acquisition Applauded By Analysts |url=https://www.forbes.com/2007/01/08/advanced-medical-optics-markets-equity-cx_jl_0108markets09.html |access-date=2026-02-26 |work=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> His third, ViaLase, is currently active; its product, a device which uses femtosecond lasers to treat glaucoma, is currently in the final stages of clinical trials.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2025-12-03 |title=ViaLase Announces First Patient Treated in IDE Clinical Trial Evaluating Its Femtosecond Laser Trabeculotomy for Open-Angle Glaucoma |url=https://www.vialase.com/vialase-announces-first-patient-treated-in-ide-clinical-trial-evaluating-its-femtosecond-laser-trabeculotomy-for-open-angle-glaucoma/ |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=Vialase |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-12-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251211182100/http://www.vialase.com/vialase-announces-first-patient-treated-in-ide-clinical-trial-evaluating-its-femtosecond-laser-trabeculotomy-for-open-angle-glaucoma/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Juhasz is the recipient of the 2002 Berthold Leibinger Innovation Prize for the development and commercialization of [[femtosecond laser]] surgical technology. He also received the 2022 [[Golden Goose Award]] from the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and [[Association of American Universities]] for introducing femtosecond laser technology to [[ophthalmology]].<ref name=":5" />

==Education==
Juhasz completed his Diploma in [[Physics]] from the [[University of Szeged]] in 1982. Four years later, he received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in Physics from the same institution.<ref name="es" /> He completed his postdoctoral education at the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the [[University of California, Irvine]] from 1987 to 1990. Later, in 2001, he obtained a [[Doctor of Science]]s degree from the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":2">{{cite web|url=https://news.uci.edu/2023/01/23/grabbing-the-golden-goose/|title=Grabbing the Golden Goose|date=23 January 2023|access-date=20 November 2023|archive-date=20 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231120070947/https://news.uci.edu/2023/01/23/grabbing-the-golden-goose/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Career==

=== Early career ===
Juhasz began his academic career in 1982 as a research assistant in the Department of External Physics at the [[Technical University of Budapest]] (BME).  In 1985, was made an [[assistant professor]]. He stayed at BME for two more years, before leaving in 1987 to complete a postdoc with the Department of Physics at the [[University of California, Irvine]]. It was during this time that Juhasz began to investigate the interactions between ultrashort [[laser]] pulses and matter.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Juhasz |first1=T. |last2=Bron |first2=W. |title=Subpicosecond-resolved polariton decay |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=November 1989 |volume=63 |issue=21 |pages=2385–2388 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.63.2385 |pmid=10040875 |bibcode=1989PhRvL..63.2385J }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bron |first1=W. E. |last2=Juhasz |first2=T. |last3=Mehta |first3=S. |title=New nonequilibrium phonon state |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=3 April 1989 |volume=62 |issue=14 |pages=1655–1658 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.62.1655 |pmid=10039730 |bibcode=1989PhRvL..62.1655B }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Smith |first1=G. O. |last2=Juhasz |first2=T. |last3=Bron |first3=W. E. |last4=Levinson |first4=Y. B. |title=Interaction of an electron-hole plasma with optical phonons in GaP |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=13 April 1992 |volume=68 |issue=15 |pages=2366–2369 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.68.2366 |pmid=10045377 |bibcode=1992PhRvL..68.2366S }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref> Three years later, in 1990, he was promoted to the role of Assistant Researcher Physicist.

=== Femtosecond lasers in corneal surgery ===
Juhasz left UC Irvine in 1994. Two years later, in 1996, he met [[Ophthalmology|ophthamologist]] Ron Kurtz at a conference in [[Toronto]]. At the time, Kurtz was collaborating with a team of researchers at the [[University of Michigan]] (UMich) on a project investigating the potential applications of [[Femtosecond laser|femotsecond lasers]] in [[Ophthalmology|ophthalmology]]. Juhasz, who was investigating the use of picosecond lasers for eye surgery, struck up a conversation with Kurtz, and soon Juhasz was invited to join the UMich team.<ref name=":2" />

Juhasz remained at UMich for eight more years, rising to the rank of [[associate professor]] in 1998.<ref name="es" /> During his time at the university, he and Kurtz developed a device that used femotsecond lasers to create a flap in the [[cornea]], a necessary first step for many kinds of eye surgery, including [[LASIK]].  At the time, corneal flaps had to be created surgically with a [[microkeratome]] knife, a process that was both painful for the patient and had an extended recovery period. Their invention, which they named IntraLASIK, allowed the procedure to be performed bladelessly, greatly reducing both the pain involved and the recovery period afterwards.<ref name=":1" /> Juhasz would go on to win the Berthold Leibinger Innovation Prize for his work in 2002.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |date=2025-07-03 |title=A surgical procedure without the surgery {{!}} University of California |url=https://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/surgical-procedure-without-surgery |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=www.universityofcalifornia.edu |language=en}}</ref>

In 1997, the two men founded the company [[IntraLase]] to commercialize IntraLASIK.<ref name=":1" /> Upon receiving FDA approval, the device became the first commercially available ophthalmic femtosecond laser.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Juhasz |first1=Tibor |last2=Kastis |first2=George A. |last3=Suárez |first3=Carlos |last4=Bor |first4=Zsolt |last5=Bron |first5=Walter E. |title=Time-resolved observations of shock waves and cavitation bubbles generated by femtosecond laser pulses in corneal tissue and water |journal=Lasers in Surgery and Medicine |date=1996 |volume=19 |issue=1 |pages=23–31 |doi=10.1002/(SICI)1096-9101(1996)19:1<23::AID-LSM4>3.0.CO;2-S |pmid=8836993 |s2cid=23193533 }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Juhasz |first1=T. |last2=Loesel |first2=F.H. |last3=Kurtz |first3=R.M. |last4=Horvath |first4=C. |last5=Bille |first5=J.F. |last6=Mourou |first6=G. |title=Corneal refractive surgery with femtosecond lasers |journal=IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics |date=1999 |volume=5 |issue=4 |pages=902–910 |doi=10.1109/2944.796309 |bibcode=1999IJSTQ...5..902J }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref> Juhasz initially served as the company's vice president for R&D until 2002, when he became its [[chief technology officer]] (CTO).<ref name=":0" /> During this time, Juhasz returned to UC Irvine, accepting the role of professor at the Gavin Herbert Eye Institute in the Department of Biomedical Engineering in 2004.<ref name="es" />  His research there showed that IntraLASIK offered enhanced safety and yields superior refractive outcomes in comparison to the conventional [[microkeratome]] method.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cabrera Fernández |first1=Delia |last2=Niazy |first2=A. M. |last3=Kurtz |first3=R. M. |last4=Djotyan |first4=G. Cabrera |last2=Niazy |first2=A. M. |last3=Kurtz |first3=R. M. |last4=Djotyan |first4=G. P. |last5=Juhasz |first5=T. |title=A Finite Element Model for Ultrafast Laser–Lamellar Keratoplasty |journal=Annals of Biomedical Engineering |date=22 March 2006 |volume=34 |issue=1 |pages=169–183 |doi=10.1007/s10439-005-9014-3 |pmid=16474919 |s2cid=26968302 }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref> Furthermore, his work established that employing femtosecond laser technology for [[corneal transplantation]] offers distinct benefits in comparison to conventional methods.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Soong |first1=H |last2=Mian |first2=S |last3=Abbasi |first3=O |last4=Juhasz |first4=T |title=Femtosecond laser–assisted posterior lamellar keratoplastyInitial studies of surgical technique in eye bank eyes |journal=Ophthalmology |date=January 2005 |volume=112 |issue=1 |pages=44–49 |doi=10.1016/j.ophtha.2004.06.037 |pmid=15629819 }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sarayba |first1=Melvin A |last2=Juhasz |first2=Tibor |last3=Chuck |first3=Roy S |last4=Ignacio |first4=Teresa S |last5=Nguyen |first5=Thao B |last6=Sweet |first6=Paula |last7=Kurtz |first7=Ronald M |title=Femtosecond Laser Posterior Lamellar Keratoplasty: A Laboratory Model |journal=Cornea |date=April 2005 |volume=24 |issue=3 |pages=328–333 |doi=10.1097/01.ico.0000138830.50112.f4 |pmid=15778607 |s2cid=33175561 }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fernández |first1=D Cabrera |last2=Niazy |first2=A M |last3=Kurtz |first3=R M |last4=Djotyan |first4=G P |last5=Juhasz |first5=T |title=Biomechanical Model of Corneal Transplantation |journal=Journal of Refractive Surgery |date=March 2006 |volume=22 |issue=3 |pages=293–302 |doi=10.3928/1081-597X-20060301-16 |pmid=16602319 }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref>

=== Femtosecond laser cataract surgery ===
In 2007, IntraLase was acquired by [[Advanced Medical Optics]] for $808 million.<ref name=":4" /> After its sale, Juhasz and Kurtz began investigating other potential ophthalmic applications of femtosecond lasers. The two collaborated with Hungarian researcher Zoltan Nagy to design and develop the first clinical [[cataract]] femtosecond laser.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hungarytoday.hu/revolutionary-hungarian-invention-used-improve-american-fighter-pilots-eyesight-31673/|title="Revolutionary" Hungarian Invention Used To Improve American Fighter Pilots' Eyesight|work=Hungary Today |date=30 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231120070939/https://hungarytoday.hu/revolutionary-hungarian-invention-used-improve-american-fighter-pilots-eyesight-31673/|archive-date=2023-11-20}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{cite journal |last1=Winkler |first1=Moritz |last2=Shoa |first2=Golroxan |last3=Xie |first3=Yilu |last4=Petsche |first4=Steven J. |last5=Pinsky |first5=Peter M. |last6=Juhasz |first6=Tibor |last7=Brown |first7=Donald J. |last8=Jester |first8=James V. |title=Three-Dimensional Distribution of Transverse Collagen Fibers in the Anterior Human Corneal Stroma |journal=Investigative Ophthalmology & Visual Science |date=5 November 2013 |volume=54 |issue=12 |pages=7293–7501 |doi=10.1167/iovs.13-13150 |pmid=24114547 |pmc=4589141 }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref> Later research by Juhasz would demonstrate that the mechanical strength of femtosecond laser [[capsulotomy]] is on par with that of manual capsulotomy, but with a significantly reduced variability in strength. Consequently, these studies significantly decreased the likelihood and rate of capsular tears and other complications.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mikula |first1=Eric R. |last2=Jester |first2=James V. |last3=Juhasz |first3=Tibor |title=Measurement of an Elasticity Map in the Human Cornea |journal=Investigative Ophthalmology & Visual Science |date=21 June 2016 |volume=57 |issue=7 |pages=3282–3286 |doi=10.1167/iovs.15-18248 |pmid=27327584 |pmc=4961063 }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mikula |first1=Eric |last2=Winkler |first2=Moritz |last3=Juhasz |first3=Tibor |last4=Brown |first4=Donald J. |last5=Shoa |first5=Golroxan |last6=Tran |first6=Stephanie |last7=Kenney |first7=M. Cristina |last8=Jester |first8=James V. |title=Axial mechanical and structural characterization of keratoconus corneas |journal=Experimental Eye Research |date=October 2018 |volume=175 |pages=14–19 |doi=10.1016/j.exer.2018.05.019 |pmid=29842851 |pmc=7324026 }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref>

Juhasz and Kurtz once again founded a company, LenSx Lasers, to commercialize their new invention.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> LenSx Lasers would eventually be acquired by [[Alcon]] for $316.5 million in 2010.<ref name=":3" /> Juhasz stayed on after the sale, serving as vice president of R&D for Alcon's LenSx division until 2016.<ref name=":0" />

During this time period, Juhasz also contributed to research in the field of corneal biomechanics{{citation needed|date=December 2023}} and in the field of the treatment of [[keratoconus]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US9095414B2/en|title=Nonlinear optical photodynamic therapy (NLO-PDT) of the cornea|access-date=2023-11-16|archive-date=2023-11-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116091713/https://patents.google.com/patent/US9095414B2/en|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chai |first1=Dongyul |last2=Juhasz |first2=Tibor |last3=Brown |first3=Donald J. |last4=Jester |first4=James V. |title=Nonlinear optical collagen cross-linking and mechanical stiffening: a possible photodynamic therapeutic approach to treating corneal ectasia |journal=Journal of Biomedical Optics |date=20 March 2013 |volume=18 |issue=3 |article-number=038003 |doi=10.1117/1.JBO.18.3.038003 |pmid=23515869 |pmc=3603223 |bibcode=2013JBO....18c8003C }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref>

=== Femtosecond laser treatment for glaucoma ===
After leaving Alcon, Juhasz turned his attention towards another potential ophthalmic use for femtosecond lasers: treating [[glaucoma]]. Juhasz had made his first attempt at developing a glaucoma treatment the mid-1990s, when he undertook a research project supported by the [[National Institutes of Health]] (NIH) that aimed to reduce [[intraocular pressure]] by establishing partial thickness channels from the front chamber to the area beneath the [[conjunctiva]] through the [[sclera]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sacks |first1=Zachary S. |last2=Kurtz |first2=Ron M. |last3=Juhasz |first3=Tibor |last4=Mourau |first4=Gerard A. |title=High precision subsurface photodisruption in human sclera |journal=Journal of Biomedical Optics |date=2002 |volume=7 |issue=3 |pages=442–450 |doi=10.1117/1.1482381 |pmid=12175295 |bibcode=2002JBO.....7..442S |doi-access=free }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1117/12.701297 |chapter=Investigation and visualization of scleral channels created with femtosecond laser in enucleated human eyes using 3D optical coherence tomography images |title=Ophthalmic Technologies XVII |date=2007 |editor-last1=Manns |editor-first1=Fabrice |last1=Chaudhary |first1=Gautam |last2=Rao |first2=Bin |last3=Chai |first3=Dongyul |author4-link=Zhongping Chen|last4=Chen |first4=Zhongping |last5=Juhasz |first5=Tibor |volume=6426 |pages=64260B |s2cid=122311420 |editor-first2=Per G. |editor-first3=Arthur |editor-first4=Bruce E. |editor-first5=Michael |editor-last2=Soederberg |editor-last3=Ho |editor-last4=Stuck |editor-last5=Belkin }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref> Although the channels proved to be efficient, his early animal experiments showed a swift healing response, which subsequently constrained the long-term efficacy of these treatments.<ref name=":8">{{cite journal |last1=Luo |title=Dispersion compensation for spectral domain optical coherence tomography by time-frequency analysis and iterative optimization |journal=Optics Continuum |date=May 2022 |volume=1 |issue=5 |pages=1117–1136 |doi=10.1364/OPTCON.455242 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":9">{{cite journal |last1=Luo |first1=Shangbang |last2=Holland |first2=Guy |last3=Khazaeinezhad |first3=Reza |journal=Scientific Reports |date=24 August 2023 |volume=13 |issue=1 |page=13861 |doi=10.1038/s41598-023-37248-0  |doi-access=free|pmid=37620338 |pmc=10449890 |bibcode=2023NatSR..1313861L }}{{primary Even at the time, Juhasz had believed that these issues could be resolved once femtosecond laser technology had sufficiently improved.<ref name=":7" /> So in 2017, Juhasz resumed his research. |last9=Juhasz |first9=Tibor |title=Femtosecond Laser Trabeculotomy in Perfused Human Cadaver Anterior Segments: A Novel, Noninvasive Approach to Glaucoma Treatment |journal=Translational Vision Science & Technology |date=25 March 2022 |volume=11 |issue=3 |page=28 |doi=10.1167/tvst.11.3.28 |pmid=35333286 |pmc=8963660 }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref>

However, by 2017, the technology had improved sufficiently to allow his team to develop a treatment.<ref name=":7"/> That same year, Juhasz founded the company ViaLase to commercialize this latest invention.<ref name=":1" />  He currently serves as the company's [[President (corporate title)|President]] and [[Chief technology officer|CTO]].<ref name=":0" />  In initial human trials, ViaLase's eponymous glaucoma treatment demonstrated a highly favorable safety record and delivered effective, long-lasting results over a two-year follow-up period.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patentscope.wipo.int/search/en/detail.jsf?docId=WO2018144477|title=WIPO - Search International and National Patent Collections|website=patentscope.wipo.int|access-date=2023-11-16|archive-date=2023-11-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116091711/https://patentscope.wipo.int/search/en/detail.jsf?docId=WO2018144477|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nagy |first1=Zoltan Z. |last2=Kranitz |first2=Kinga |last3=Ahmed |first3=Iqbal Ike K. |last4=De Francesco |first4=Ticiana |last5=Mikula |first5=Eric |last6=Juhasz |first6=Tibor |title=First-in-Human Safety Study of Femtosecond Laser Image-Guided Trabeculotomy for Glaucoma Treatment |journal=Ophthalmology Science |date=December 2023 |volume=3 |issue=4 |article-number=100313 |doi=10.1016/j.xops.2023.100313 |pmid=37363134 |pmc=10285639 }}{{primary source inline|date=December 2023}}</ref>
